title: Regional circuit-sweeper observability and adaptive shed playbook
creator: Priya Singh
description: Build a cross-region observability surface and operational playbook that surfaces correlated golden signals, maps circuit states across regions, and drives adaptive load-shedding decisions. Deliverables: (1) a set of Grafana dashboards that correlate token-level latency SLIs (p50/p95/p99) with admission rate, KV cache hit rate, queue depth, and circuit state timelines per region and per priority; (2) a regional topology panel that visualizes route/replica affinities, active fallbacks, and recent migration events; (3) a synthetic microburst harness dashboard showing admission/evict behavior and model variant fallback under controlled bursts; (4) an on-call playbook (runbook) describing investigation steps, automated rollback/circuit-sweeper triggers, and manual escalation paths.
background: We have recurring incidents where tail latencies and admission spikes in one region silently cascade to other regions due to aggressive failover or route migration. Current dashboards are region-isolated and don't show causal correlations between admission pressure, circuit states, and per-token SLI regressions. We need a combined observability + playbook surface so on-call and SREs can quickly diagnose and execute safe shed/rollback strategies.
goals: Deliver a correlation dashboard that shows token-p99 vs admission rate vs KV hit vs active circuit state across regions within one view
Expose per-priority failure modes (high, default, low) so we can validate graceful degradation behavior
Implement synthetic microburst panel with controlled traffic generator results to validate shed thresholds and hysteresis
Publish an on-call playbook that codifies circuit-sweeper heuristics and fallback run steps
scope_in: Grafana panels and Loki traces that join token-level SLI histograms with admission/circuit metrics
A single-pane regional topology visualization showing active fallback routes and last-failed timestamp
Playbook document stored in Confluence with TL;DR quick actions and escalation matrix
Synthetic microburst harness wiring to existing chaos infra (synthetic-traffic job)
out_of_scope: Implementing new admission control algorithms (prototype only; follow-up task required)
Long-term automated rollback automation (will be a separate RFC/epic)
Major schema changes to telemetry pipelines — we will leverage existing event fields
acceptance_criteria: Dashboard shows correlated signals for a three-hour window across two regions and can be filtered by route and priority
On-call runbook contains reproducible investigation steps and checklists with example queries and decision thresholds
Synthetic microburst harness produces repeatable plots demonstrating shed behaviour at configured rates and documents where hysteresis prevented flip-flop
Dashboards surface at least one actionable alert rule (p99>threshold + admission surge + low KV hit) with a suggested severity mapping
tasks: Instrument join keys for traces: ensure request_id, route_id, shard_id, priority are present on admission and circuit events
Create Grafana dashboard: regional-correlation-views (panels: token-latency-histograms, admission-rate, kv-hit, queue-depth, circuit-state-timeline)
Build regional topology panel using service discovery metadata and last-fallback timestamps
Wire synthetic microburst job to dashboard: add panels for synthetic admission, shed decisions, and model-variant fallbacks
Author Confluence playbook: symptoms -> quick checks -> automated mitigations -> manual rollback steps -> postmortem artifacts
Add alerting rules and document noise threshold tuning; propose to on-call rotation
Run tabletop exercise with SREs and on-call to validate playbook and dashboard usability
